basis: Developmental disability and brachydactyly define the syndrome; obesity occurs in 4/6. Single-patient visceral findings do not establish common involvement.
Isolated bilateral shortening of toe bones.
Hair and nail dysplasia, with alopecia and nail dystrophy in 8/8; absent eyelashes do not establish eye damage.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability are common defining features; other organ malformations vary with the duplicated segment.
Cognitive and autonomic dysfunction support neurologic classification; fatigue and myalgia do not establish muscle injury. Immune causation is not established.
Brain malformations and cutaneous vascular malformations define MCAP; syndactyly/polydactyly occur in 80-99%, with joint hypermobility in 30-79%.
Acute nicotine poisoning causes central and autonomic nervous system dysfunction; vomiting and skin absorption do not establish gastrointestinal or skin injury.
Joint instability and skin fragility define the disorder; sensory/peripheral neuropathy occurs in 30-79%. Vascular and gastrointestinal lesions are occasional.
Broad neoplasm category arising in mesenchymal soft tissue or bone; additional organ sites depend on the individual tumour subtype.
Disordered extracellular pyrophosphate metabolism produces arterial calcification and stenosis. Renal artery disease remains vascular; rickets is occasional.
Nonsyndromic prelingual sensorineural hearing loss in 6/6.
Alzheimer disease subtype defined by progressive cerebral neurodegeneration and dementia.
Tumour originates in sinonasal olfactory epithelium, within the airway axis. Orbital or intracranial extension is not established as common across patients.
Severe alpha-chain deficiency causes fetal anemia; heart failure occurs in 80-99% and hydrocephalus in 30-79%. Hepatomegaly alone does not establish liver injury.
Joubert syndrome defines a cerebellar/brainstem developmental disorder; subtype-specific common retinal, renal or hepatic damage is not established here.
Familial cortical myoclonus and epilepsy; tremor occurs in 8/10.
Cystic renal dysplasia, encephalocele and limb malformations define the phenotype; hepatic ductal-plate malformation/fibrosis is common (>30%) in Meckel syndrome.
Primary carcinoma of the uterine cervix, a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Defined neurodevelopmental disorder with developmental delay, intellectual disability and autism-spectrum features.
Inherited retinal dysfunction or degeneration, encompassing stationary night blindness and retinitis pigmentosa.
Acute cerebral dysfunction with encephalopathy in 3/3; vomiting and abdominal pain are symptoms without demonstrated gastrointestinal injury.
Primary skeletal muscle channelopathy/myopathy. Respiratory weakness and ophthalmoplegia reflect affected muscles; common intrinsic lung or eye injury is unestablished.
Pelvic mesenchymal soft-tissue overgrowth; urinary tract compression with hydronephrosis occurs in roughly 40%. Constipation alone does not establish bowel injury.
Retinal degeneration with chorioretinal atrophy in 20/20. Respiratory infections lack evidence of common lasting airway damage.
Congenital epidermal keratinization disorder, with erythroderma in 6/6. Ectropion is reported in one patient; prevalence of at least 30% is not established.
